title: Cartesian geometric descent and effective groupoids in spaces
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use spaces and coherent diagrams of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a small simplicial space $X_\bullet$ write $|X_\bullet|=\operatorname{colim}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}X_n$. The map $X_0\to|X_\bullet|$ is surjective on $\pi_0$. Geometric realization commutes with finite products of simplicial spaces. If a natural transformation $Y_\bullet\to X_\bullet$ has a pullback naturality square for every arrow of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, then $Y_n\to|Y_\bullet|$ over $X_n\to|X_\bullet|$ is a pullback square for each $n$. For a nonempty ordered subset $S\subseteq[n]$, write $G_S=G_{|S|-1}$ with restriction induced by increasing enumeration. A simplicial space $G_\bullet$ is called a groupoid object if, for every union $[n]=S\cup T$ with one common vertex, its restriction map $G_n\to G_S\times_{G_{S\cap T}}G_T$ is an equivalence. Every groupoid object in spaces is effective: its augmentation $G_0\to|G_\bullet|$ is surjective on $\pi_0$, and $G_n\simeq G_0\times_{|G_\bullet|}\cdots\times_{|G_\bullet|}G_0$ with $n+1$ factors, naturally with the simplicial operators. In particular $G_1\simeq G_0\times_{|G_\bullet|}G_0$. For a commutative square $Y\to Y\prime$ over $X\to X\prime$, let $q:Y\to X\times_{X\prime}Y\prime$ be its pullback comparison. If $T\to X$ is surjective on $\pi_0$ and $q$ is an equivalence on every homotopy fiber over every point of $T$, then $q$ is an equivalence.

source.place: HTT Theorem 6.1.0.6(2),(3)(iv), Proposition 6.1.2.6(4), Theorem 6.1.3.9(4), and Lemmas 5.5.8.4, 5.5.8.11 with Remark 5.5.8.12. Applications and fiberwise detection: Gepner-Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4, Lemma 5.2.9, Proposition 5.3.6 and proof of Theorem 5.6.2. Both sources read directly; local reading copies are in the delivery sandbox, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Let $X_\bullet$ be a small simplicial space with its realization cocone. The dual cocone criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that restriction from $\operatorname{Map}(|X_\bullet|,D)$ to the space of coherent cocones from $X_\bullet$ to $D$ is an equivalence. Take $D=\{0,1\}$ discrete. A map from a Kan complex $A$ to $D$ is exactly a function on $\pi_0(A)$: edges force equal values, and all higher simplices in $D$ are uniquely forced. Every point of $X_n$ maps into the same realization component as its restriction to any vertex in $X_0$, by the given cocone. If a realization component missed $X_0$, its characteristic function would be a nonzero map $|X_\bullet|\to D$ restricting to the zero map on every $X_n$. These restrictions form the zero coherent cocone, since coherence into a discrete target is unique. The cocone criterion would identify the characteristic function with the zero map, a contradiction. Thus $X_0\to|X_\bullet|$ is surjective on $\pi_0$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, first assertion: component surjectivity of the realization.

proof.text: We compute realization by a strict bisimplicial model. The Kan model structure in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] is a combinatorial simplicial model category, as follows from its stated generators and [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]. Indeed, simplicial sets are complete and cocomplete degreewise; every simplicial set is the filtered union of its subobjects generated by finitely many nondegenerate simplices. A map from one such finite object is determined by finitely many simplex images and finitely many face equations, so its ordinary Hom functor preserves filtered colimits. These finite objects form a small family up to isomorphism, proving local finite presentability. The boundary and horn inclusions in the Kan-model statement are small generating sets. Tensor, cotensor and enrichment are Cartesian product and the simplicial function complex. A pushout product of monomorphisms is degreewise injective; if either factor is trivial, the cited anodyne pushout-product statement (and symmetry) makes it trivial. This verifies the simplicial-model hypothesis. Now take $K=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and the discrete simplicial category $I=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], its coherent nerve is its ordinary nerve and the counit $\mathfrak C[N(I)]\to I$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence: $I$ is locally Kan, all Joyal simplicial sets are cofibrant, and the stated Quillen equivalence gives this derived counit. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] to this counit and the Kan model category. It presents every coherent simplicial space by a strict simplicial diagram $Z:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$ of Kan complexes, and computes its coherent colimit by a fibrant replacement of the enriched colimit of a projectively cofibrant replacement of $Z$. The presentation includes transformations. Strict products of the Kan-valued diagrams represent their pointwise space products: the simplicial function complex into a product is the product of the function complexes, and the coherent nerve preserves products as a right adjoint.

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational product compatibility; agent expansion through the simplicial-model comparison of HTT 4.2.4.4 and an explicit free bar resolution, avoiding the cyclic sifted-index interfaces.

proof.text: Here is the required projective replacement calculation, for any small ordinary category $C$ and strict $Z:C\to\mathsf{sSet}$. Form the simplicial diagram of free $C$-diagrams $P_k=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_k}C(c_k,-)\times Z(c_0)$, with faces composing adjacent arrows (the first acts on $Z(c_0)$) and degeneracies inserting identities. Put $QZ=\int^{[k]}P_k\times\Delta^k$. This coend is formed degreewise; in degree $r$ its relations identify $(p,t:[r]\to[k])$ with $P(t)(p)$, so it is the diagonal of $P$. Filter this coend by the outer dimension $k$. The new summands are exactly chains containing no identity arrow, and their attaching maps are the free diagrams on $Z(c_0)\times\partial\Delta^k\hookrightarrow Z(c_0)\times\Delta^k$, based at $c_k$; their faces are the displayed composition maps. These are monomorphisms, hence cofibrations by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The free-diagram generators and projective-model description in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] make every such free map a projective cofibration (decompose its underlying monomorphism into boundary cells and apply the free functor). Thus $QZ$ is projectively cofibrant. The augmentation $QZ(c)\to Z(c)$ composes the chain ending in $c$. It is an objectwise weak equivalence: append $c$ and its last arrow to every chain to obtain an extra last degeneracy. In realization its contraction sends the barycentric coordinates $(t_0,\ldots,t_k)$ to $((1-s)t_0,\ldots,(1-s)t_k,s)$ on this appended chain. At $s=0$ it is the identity, and at $s=1$ it is augmentation followed by the summand $(c,1_c)$. Explicitly augment the outer simplicial object by $P_{-1}(c)=Z(c)$ and write $h_k$ for the operation appending the arrow $c_k\to c$ and then $1_c$, with $h_{-1}(z)$ the summand $(c,1_c,z)$. Its identities are $d_{k+1}h_k=1$, $d_i h_k=h_{k-1}d_i$ for $0\leq i\leq k$ (where $d_0:P_0(c)\to Z(c)$ is augmentation), $s_i h_k=h_{k+1}s_i$ for $0\leq i\leq k$, and $s_{k+1}h_k=h_{k+1}h_k$. For the last face one composes $c_k\to c$ with $1_c$ and recovers the original last arrow; for every other face or degeneracy, deletion, composition or insertion occurs before that last arrow. These formulas prove that the barycentric homotopy descends through the face and degeneracy relations. At its final endpoint the remaining first-face relations compose the whole chain and give $h_{-1}$ after augmentation; on the section the appended arrows are identities, so the homotopy is constant. [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] supplies the realization/coend and product identifications, so this is a homotopy between the realized maps and proves the required weak equivalence. If replacement is required to be a trivial fibration, factor $QZ\to Z$ as a trivial cofibration $QZ\to Q'Z$ followed by a fibration; two-out-of-three makes the latter trivial. Both sources are projectively cofibrant. The colimit functor preserves this trivial cofibration, since its constant-diagram right adjoint preserves objectwise fibrations and trivial fibrations. Therefore either replacement computes the same derived colimit. Finally $\operatorname{colim}_C C(c_k,-)=*$, since every element is the image of $1_{c_k}$. Interchanging the two explicit colimit quotients gives $\operatorname{colim}_C QZ=\operatorname{BK}_C Z$, with its usual cocone. For $C=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus] gives the natural weak equivalence $\operatorname{BK}_C Z\to\operatorname{diag}Z$. By the preceding model comparison, $|X_\bullet|$ is consequently represented by $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}\operatorname{diag}Z$, where [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products] supplies this natural Kan replacement. All these comparisons retain their cocones and are natural in $Z$.

proof.text: Take strict Kan-valued presentations $Z^{(a)}$ of a finite family $X^{(a)}_\bullet$ using step 2. Diagonal commutes with their products degreewise: $\operatorname{diag}(\prod_a Z^{(a)})=\prod_a\operatorname{diag}Z^{(a)}$. By [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], the canonical comparison $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(\prod_a\operatorname{diag}Z^{(a)})\to\prod_a\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}\operatorname{diag}Z^{(a)}$ is an isomorphism. Step 3 identifies these two objects with the realization of the product and the product of the realizations. Naturality of the bar-to-diagonal comparison and of the Kan-replacement unit makes its projection to each factor the original realization comparison; hence it is the required canonical equivalence. For zero factors the strict diagram is constant at the point, its diagonal is a point, and the terminal-object clause of the same Kan-replacement statement gives the nullary comparison.

source.place: Paragraph 2, foundational product compatibility; agent expansion through the simplicial-model comparison of HTT 4.2.4.4 and an explicit free bar resolution, avoiding the cyclic sifted-index interfaces.

proof.text: Let $Y_\bullet\to X_\bullet$ have pullback naturality squares on every arrow. The statement of [lem-coef-coherent-diagram-coyoneda] gives colimits in the coherent functor category pointwise, so the transformation extends to a morphism of the two realization cocones. Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-colimit-descent-criterion] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal S$. The space category is presentable with finite limits, and [lem-coef-space-universal-colimits-cartesian-pushouts] supplies universal colimits and the required gluing of cartesian arrows under pushouts. The hypotheses on the squares over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ are exactly the criterion’s cartesian-edge hypotheses, while both realization cocones are colimiting. The criterion therefore says that the square at each cone vertex is a pullback, namely $Y_n\simeq X_n\times_{|X_\bullet|}|Y_\bullet|$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, first application of HTT Theorem 6.1.3.9 to cartesian realization.

proof.text: Let $G_\bullet$ be a groupoid object and put $H_n=G_{n+1}$, with operators extending each monotone map by fixing a new last vertex. Restriction to the first $n+1$ vertices gives $\alpha:H_\bullet\to G_\bullet$. For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, choose $i\in[m]$ and set $j=\theta(i)$. The unions $[n+1]=[n]\cup\{j,n+1\}$ and $[m+1]=[m]\cup\{i,m+1\}$ have one common vertex. The defining groupoid condition therefore gives $G_{n+1}\simeq G_n\times_{G_0}G_1$ and $G_{m+1}\simeq G_m\times_{G_0}G_1$, using the vertices $j$ and $i$ respectively. The extended $\theta$ restricts to the identity between these ordered two-element subsets. Hence the naturality square of $\alpha$ is the square with top row $(G_n\times_{G_0}G_1)\to G_n$, bottom row $(G_m\times_{G_0}G_1)\to G_m$, and vertical maps $\theta^*\times1$ and $\theta^*:G_n\to G_m$; here $G_n\to G_0$ is the vertex $j$, $G_m\to G_0$ is the vertex $i$, and $i^*\theta^*=j^*$. By pasting of pullbacks, $G_n\times_{G_m}(G_m\times_{G_0}G_1)\simeq G_n\times_{G_0}G_1$, compatibly with both projections. It is a pullback. This calculation permits every $\theta$, including noninjective ones.

source.place: Paragraph 2, groupoid condition implies the right-shift transformation is cartesian; HTT Proposition 6.1.2.6(4).

proof.text: Let $\Delta_\infty$ have all finite ordinals $J$, including $\varnothing$, and maps $J\sqcup\{\infty\}\to J'\sqcup\{\infty\}$ fixing the new greatest element. Define $F:N(\Delta_\infty)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ by $F(J)=G(J\sqcup\{\infty\})$. Its restriction along $i^{\mathrm{op}}:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta_\infty^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $i$ includes the NONEMPTY ordinals and extends maps to fix $\infty$, is $H_\bullet$. There is an ordinary adjunction $i\dashv U$ with $U(J)=J\sqcup\{\infty\}$: restriction to the ordinary elements gives the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta_\infty}(iA,J)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(A,UJ)$. On a morphism, $U$ is its underlying monotone map between the nonempty extended ordinals; thus the bijection respects composition. Taking opposites gives $U^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv i^{\mathrm{op}}$. Since $\varnothing$ is initial in $\Delta_\infty$, it is final in the opposite, so [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] gives a colimit cocone on $F$ with vertex $F(\varnothing)=G_0$. Its edges are restriction to the last vertex. By [lem-coef-infinity-right-adjoint-reindexing], restricting this cocone along the right adjoint $i^{\mathrm{op}}$ gives a colimit cocone on $H_\bullet$, with the same vertex $G_0$. Write $B=|G_\bullet|$. To specify the augmented transformation, extend $G_\bullet$ by its realization cocone to $\overline G:N(\Delta_+)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$, with $\overline G(\varnothing)=B$. On finite ordinals, including the empty one, the natural inclusions $J\hookrightarrow J\sqcup\{\infty\}$ give, after applying $\overline G$ contravariantly, a coherent transformation $\overline G(J\sqcup\{\infty\})\to\overline G(J)$. Its nonempty restriction is $\alpha$, its component at the empty ordinal is the original $G_0\to B$, and its source augmentation is restriction to the last vertex. Naturality of the inclusions supplies all the compatibility homotopies used here. Step 6 gives cartesianness on the unaugmented diagrams. Applying step 5 therefore gives the canonical $G_{n+1}\simeq G_n\times_B G_0$. Induct on $n$, starting with $G_0$ (one factor): the displayed equivalence adjoins its last vertex and gives the comparison of $G_{n+1}$ with $n+2$ factors from that of $G_n$ with $n+1$ factors. Thus every canonical vertex comparison $G_n\to G_0^{\times_B(n+1)}$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Paragraph 2, right-shift/split-augmentation effectiveness argument, expanded via HTT Lemmas 6.1.3.16–17.

proof.text: Naturality in the simplicial operators. Let $\overline G:N(\Delta_+)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ be the augmented diagram of step 7, with $\overline G(\varnothing)=B$. For each $[n]$, the objects of $\Delta_+$ of dimension at most $0$ over $[n]$ are $\varnothing\to[n]$ and the $n+1$ vertex inclusions $\{k\}\to[n]$, with the unique maps $\varnothing\to\{k\}$. The restriction of $\overline G$ to (the opposite of) this slice is the diagram of $n+1$ copies of the augmentation $G_0\to B$, and $\overline G$ itself supplies the cone on it with apex $G_n$: its legs are the vertex restrictions $k^*:G_n\to G_0$ and the augmentation $G_n\to B$, and its commutation homotopies are simplices of $\overline G$. A limit of this diagram is the iterated pullback $G_0\times_B\cdots\times_BG_0$ with $n+1$ factors, obtained by adjoining one leg at a time; the comparison induced by the cone is exactly the canonical vertex comparison of step 7, so it is an equivalence and the cone is limiting. Hence $\overline G$ exhibits every $G_n$ as the limit of its restriction to the vertices and the augmentation, that is, $\overline G$ is a right Kan extension of its restriction to dimensions at most $0$ (the Cech-nerve condition of HTT Proposition 6.1.2.11(1)). This is the asserted naturality: for $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, precomposition with $\theta$ sends the vertex $\{k\}\to[m]$ to $\{\theta(k)\}\to[n]$, so $k^*\theta^*=\theta(k)^*$ by the coherence of $\overline G$; therefore under the equivalences above $\theta^*$ is the map selecting coordinates $\theta(0),\ldots,\theta(m)$, with repetitions and omissions for noninjective or nonsurjective $\theta$, and all higher compatibilities are the higher simplices of the single coherent diagram $\overline G$. No further choice is made. In particular $G_1\simeq G_0\times_BG_0$; component surjectivity of $G_0\to B$ follows from step 1.

source.place: Paragraph 2, canonical Cech comparison and its coherence; HTT Proposition 6.1.2.11, (2) implies (1), and Proposition 6.1.3.19 (effectiveness).

proof.text: Given a commutative square and its pullback comparison $q:Y\to P=X\times_{X'}Y'$, suppose $T\to X$ is surjective on $\pi_0$ and $q$ is an equivalence on homotopy fibers over points of $T$. Every vertex of $X$ is connected by a path to the image of a vertex of $T$; concatenating with this path and its reverse identifies the corresponding homotopy fibers of $Y$ and $P$, compatibly with $q$. Thus $q$ is an equivalence on every fiber over $X$. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] with base map $1_X$ to conclude that $q$ is an equivalence. If $T$ is empty, surjectivity forces $X$ empty and the conclusion is immediate.

split_report.summary: Nine-step proof with statement unchanged.
